    Adjusted PIT-Wasserstein: A Calibration Metric for Probabilistic Estimators

    A dispersion calibration metric for probabilistic estimators, disentangled from bias and sharpness. Originally published as Supplementary Appendix 2 of Challen & Danon (2025), “Instantaneous Reproduction Number Estimation From Modelled Incidence”; this repository is the extension into a standalone paper.

    Core concepts

    The paper defines three metrics for assessing probabilistic estimators and differentiating between, bias, dispersion miscalibration, and skill-spread decoupling.

    Baseline PIT-Wasserstein (Upit*U^*_{pit})

    Bpit=1n∑i=1n|ui−ranki|B_{pit} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n{|u_i - rank_i|}

    Where ranki=(i−0.5)/nrank_i = (i-0.5)/n and uiu_i are the PIT values.

    • Range: [0, 0.5]. Zero = perfect calibration and zero bias.
    • Property: Symmetric on log-calibration for a given bias.
    • Validated: Dependent on bias, dispersion calibration and sharpness in simulation.

    Adjusted PIT-Wasserstein (Upit*U^*_{pit})

    Upit=1n∑i=1n|ui,adj−ranki|U_{pit} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n{|u_{i,adj} - rank_i|}

    Where ranki=(i−0.5)/nrank_i = (i-0.5)/n and ui,adju_{i,adj} are the bias-adjusted PIT values.

    • Range: [0, 0.5]. Zero = perfect calibration.
    • Property: Symmetric on log-calibration — conservative and overconfident estimators of equal magnitude score equally.
    • Validated: Independent of bias and sharpness in simulation.

    Directed PIT-Wasserstein (Dpit*D^*_{pit})

    $$D_{pit} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n{(u_{i,adj} - rank_i) \times \sgn(0.5-rank_i)}$$

    • Range: [-0.25, +0.25]
    • Direction: Positive = overconfident (U-shaped PIT histogram); Negative = conservative (dome-shaped).

    All three metrics are accompanied by significance tests which answer the question, given an estimator and a known set of true values is there any evidence of bias or miscalibration.

    Literature context

    Closest existing work; all of it is in the pit-wasserstein Zotero collection, and references/literature-review.md has the detail.

    Paper Metric Difference from Upit*U^*_{pit}
    Wessel et al. (2025) arXiv:2506.13687 MCB = mean |sorted PIT - uniform| No bias adjustment. Used as regularisation during training, not evaluation.
    Wilks (2018) QJRMS 144:76–88 Miscalibration penalty (deviations of PIT from uniform) First PIT-uniformity penalty. Qualitative/binned, not Wasserstein.
    Kuleshov, Fenner & Ermon (2018) ICML PCE = sup-norm |PIT CDF - uniform CDF| Sup-norm (KS-style), not L1/Wasserstein. No bias adjustment.
    Dheur & Ben Taieb (2023) ICML PCE (same definition) Large-scale empirical study of PCE.
    Gneiting, Balabdaoui & Raftery (2007) JRSS-B — Canonical PIT/calibration/sharpness framework.
    Hamill (2001) MWR 129:550–560 — Rank histograms for ensemble verification.
    Brockwell (2007) Stat. Prob. Lett. — Universal residuals / PIT residuals.
    Podsztavek et al. (2024) ESANN — ML classification of PIT histogram shapes.
    Arrieta-Ibarra et al. (2022) JMLR 23 — Survey of calibration metrics; reliability diagrams.
    Panaretos & Zemel (2019) Annu. Rev. Stat. Appl. — Wasserstein distances in statistics.
    Bosse et al. (2024) arXiv:2205.07090 — scoringutils has the AD test for PIT uniformity, no Wasserstein calibration metric.

    Summary of novelty

    The adjusted PIT-Wasserstein (Upit*U^*_{pit}) appears to be genuinely novel as a standalone evaluative calibration metric because it uniquely combines:

    1. Bias adjustment before PIT uniformity assessment (no other metric does this)
    2. Wasserstein/L1 distance rather than sup-norm (PCE) or binning (reliability diagrams)
    3. Signed direction (Dpit*D^*_{pit}) distinguishing overconfidence from over-conservatism
    4. Validation showing it is independent of bias and sharpness

    The closest existing metrics (Wessel et al.’s MCB, Kuleshov et al.’s PCE) measure raw PIT uniformity without de-biasing, so represent calibration as both bias and dispersion calibration and are not informative on dispersion miscalibration in the presence of bias.
